name: Ass & Hip Archetypes
tagline: Thirteen archetypes. One carries Mass, one carries Motion — and in v8 the Mass terms split again into FULLNESS and HANDFEEL.
body:
Mass Archetype is the substance of the ass: size, cheek fullness, density, softness, firmness, bounce potential. Motion Archetype is its behaviour: motion pattern, shelf shape, recoil, sway, back-to-ass transition. Single-archetype girls inherit both from their one pick. Each archetype carries mechanical modifiers that feed the automatic outputs.

V8 REMOVES THIS SYSTEM RATHER THAN REFINING IT, and the Archive briefly filed the opposite. The Mass × Motion pairing is not being split into finer Mass terms — IT IS BEING RETIRED WHOLE, because it asked one category to answer geometry, quantity, touch, arrangement and behaviour at once, and then conscripted HIPS, which have no say in any of them.

THE THIRTEEN SURVIVE AS LEGACY MODIFIER FAMILIES. Their useful traits may now be selected independently instead of staying trapped inside indivisible packages. Shrine contributes PAWG FULLNESS without requiring Heavy Settle. Minx contributes DART to an enormous ass without forcing it to be small. Anchor contributes DENSE HANDFEEL without requiring Grounded Drive. Recoil contributes SPRINGY without Snapback, or Snapback without dictating scale. BUBBLE and DEVOTEE are promoted into the two foundational Shapes, and DEVOTEE IS RETIRED AS A NAME because it made anatomy sound like a relationship role.

THE ANATOMY SURVIVES; THE FILING MISTAKE DOES NOT. See v8-lower-body for the seven-layer replacement, and c-quinn-desk for what the old pairing line cost the Archive before the document arrived.
rules: Bubble — high pop, plush recoil, round mass
Devotee — deep undercurve, grounding plush, built to be held
Sway — wide grounded hips, rolling motion
Anchor — DENSE HANDFEEL. Grounded, solid, throne-coded. A v8 handfeel term, NOT a Pillar
Shrine — PAWG FULLNESS, top of the mass scale. Dramatic sculpted dome, worship lines
Jaunty — dangerous bounce, upper pop, brat-catching curve
Minx — tight, sharp lift, compact under pressure
Idol — curve-presence, sculpted upper flare, worship-commanding
Command — double-shelf mass, vertical gap always visible
Drama — theatrical sweep, spotlight gap, showstopper arc
